title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
slides: Why did Meta suddenly back down on AI scraping?
New UK business terms were meant to take effect imminently
Publishers pushed back hard — and Meta quietly paused them
If you publish content, Meta still wants your data eventually
Check your terms now — silence from Meta may be temporary
thread_text:
1. Meta's Quiet Retreat

Meta paused new UK business terms for AI scraping just before they were set to take effect. Publishers pushed back hard, and Meta backed down—for now.

2. Publishers Fight Back

UK publishers mounted fierce opposition to Meta's data scraping plans, forcing the company to quietly hit pause on the new terms.

3. Terms on Hold

The new business terms were meant to take effect imminently, but Meta halted them after publisher backlash. The pause is temporary, but the message is clear.

4. Data Still Wanted

Meta still plans to scrape your data eventually. The pause is a tactical retreat, not a surrender. If you publish content, expect the pressure to return.

5. Check Your Terms Now

Don't wait for Meta to act. Review your current terms and prepare for the next round. Silence from Meta is temporary—your content is still in their sights.
